definition: Hardware multithreading lets one core keep more than one thread's state and switch between them, often to hide a stall such as a cache miss. The threads share the core's execution units. It is a hardware technique, separate from the operating system scheduling many threads onto many cores.
details: Simultaneous multithreading is the common form, where the threads share a core's execution units in the same cycle.
examples: A core running two hardware threads so one can proceed while the other waits on memory
